- Rex's leg 'slams', and the catch is absorbed whole (recoilAbsorbedC 21,496 kg·m/s).

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced in my own clone with main (960fdfa), round 1 (4ea43ef) and the branch (54fadb8) side by side. On main, a bolted pull with the power on at the default dial has no courtesy ceiling (rattle preset 88,015 kg-force, plaster never). Main had a ceiling only at a 10^6 kg dial: plaster at 481,060 kg-force, about 479,000 just under it. Round 1 had no ceiling at either dial. The branch has a ceiling from his steps at both dials (plaster about 86,500 and 86,300; the ceiling sits just under at about 86,000), and its rattle preset is 15,841 at both. So at the default dial the ceiling is new, not something that comes back. The README's 'What moved' says 'the courtesy ceiling comes back from them: about 86,000 kg-force at the default dial (95%; `main` had none ...)', which contradicts itself in one sentence. The Review history entry says 'has a courtesy ceiling again (about 86,000 kg-force at the default dial)', which gives the same wrong impression. 'What moved' compares with main, and the owner never saw round 1. The wording likely came from round 2's suggested fix ('so the bolted pull's ceiling and presets come back'). The pull request's decision 4 is worded correctly ('main: none, from the rope's pull back'), so only the README is affected. This is a wrong claim in owner-facing text, but the same sentence corrects it, so it is minor.

findings.title: The page tells readers the lab ignores a pull's shaking 'as before the power existed', a reference to the lab's version history that a reader can't parse and that reads as a claim about canon
findings.location: src/app.html: the hazard-list line for the pull with the power off ('not counted with They take their own recoil off (as before the power existed)'), pullNoShake's bolted branch, and the card 'The courtesy ceiling and the not-so-heroic presets' in src/static-data.js
findings.evidence: State {action:'pull', ownRecoil:false} (and every-power-off, friction or Bolted), any effort. The 'Where each hazard starts' list reads: 'Ground shaking: not counted with They take their own recoil off (as before the power existed).' With Bolted on, the effort box reads: '...With They take their own recoil off the lab doesn't count a pull's ground shaking (as before the power existed), so a quick, hard pull may shake the ground more than the effort box says.' The card reads: 'With it off the lab counts no pull's shaking, as before the power existed: ...'. git history: the pull had no shake model before commit 9340a1c (pull request B, which added the power), so the phrase means 'as in an older version of this page'. On the page nothing explains that. In canon the power is part of who Rex and Ollie are (CLAUDE.md, 'Default powers'), so 'before the power existed' can be read as a claim that there was a time without it. The phrase appears in every powers-off pull view: 15 of my 30 dumped pull views with ownRecoil off.
findings.expected: Reader-facing text should say what the lab does and why, not which version of the lab it matches. The owner's standard asks for plain copy a general reader can follow and for no unsupported canon claims.
findings.fix: Drop the parenthetical in all three places, or replace it with the reason: 'Ground shaking: not counted with They take their own recoil off (a steady load the lab doesn't judge).' / '...the lab doesn't count a pull's ground shaking, so a quick, hard pull may shake the ground more than the effort box says.' / card: 'With it off the lab counts no pull's shaking: ...'. Engine and data.js comments can keep it.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on the rendered page. The parenthetical shows in every pull view with the power off. It is in the effort box when bolted, in the 'Where each hazard starts' list ('Ground shaking: not counted with They take their own recoil off (as before the power existed).'), and in the courtesy-ceiling card, which is on every view. 'git log -S' shows round 2 (54fadb8) introduced it. Main's copy for the same state just said 'the lab counts a pull's ground shaking only with They take their own recoil on', with no such reference. The phrase means 'as the lab did before the ownRecoil switch was added' (pull request B), which is development history a page reader has never seen and can't parse. It is also no reason: the real reason is to keep the powers-off results identical to main, and the README rightly says 'as on `main`'. In-world it can be read as a claim that there was a time before the power, while canon makes it a default power from their infinite source. CLAUDE.md says not to invent canon, and the page tone must be plain and readable for a general audience. The page's honest caveat ('so a quick, hard pull may shake the ground more than the effort box says') stays without the phrase. This is a real copy defect, minor: no number is wrong.

findings.title: The courtesy-ceiling card says a bolted pull with the power off 'all-out takes a fraction of a second', with no qualifier; at low dials it takes seconds
findings.location: src/static-data.js, card 'The courtesy ceiling and the not-so-heroic presets' (rendered in the page's assumptions cards)
findings.evidence: Card text: 'With it off the lab counts no pull's shaking, as before the power existed: his footing takes the rope's pull back as a steady load over seconds, or his bolts do over the pull, which all-out takes a fraction of a second, so a quick bolted pull may shake the ground more than it says.' Engine, P.pull(ctx({anchor:'bolted', ownRecoil:false, F: kg·g}), obj): at the page's default dial a car takes 0.312 s (true there). At a 3,000 kg dial a car takes 1.72 s, a piano 1.60 s and a bus 2.96 s; at 10,000 kg a bus takes 1.60 s. The Pull tab itself gives the real time ('over the 1.72 s the pull takes all-out' at 3 t), and README Known limits qualifies it ('0.31 s for a car at the default dial'). Only the card states it as a rule.
findings.expected: A card that explains the model should not state a dial-dependent figure as a rule. The bolted pull's all-out time depends on the dial and the load: a fraction of a second at the page's default dial, seconds at a few tonnes.
findings.fix: '...or his bolts do over the pull, which all-out can take only a fraction of a second (0.31 s for a car at the page's default dial), so a quick bolted pull may shake the ground more than it says.'

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced, and the problem is wider than the finding says: the card's claim fails even at the page's default dial. The card 'The courtesy ceiling and the not-so-heroic presets' always shows the same text, and it says a bolted pull with the power off 'all-out takes a fraction of a second'. The engine (P.pull, bolted, ownRecoil off) gives, at the default dial (90,718 kg-force), times of 0.26 to 0.94 s for the light Pull-tab objects. Heavy ones that are also on the Pull tab take longer: locomotive 2.06 s, C-17 2.08 s, Boeing 777 2.37 s. At a 3,000 kg dial a car takes 1.72 s, a bus 2.96 s and a semi 5.40 s. The Pull tab itself prints 'over the 2.06 s the pull takes all-out' for the locomotive, so the card and the tab contradict each other on the same page. That is a contradiction between page text and the engine's numbers. The card's point (a bolted pull can be quick, so shaking may be understated) is right, but the claim needs qualifying. README line 144 makes the same unconditional claim ('which all-out takes a fraction of a second (0.31 s for a car at the default dial)'), and the same qualifier fixes it there. Minor: the caveat's direction is right, but the stated rule is false for some objects and dials.
